title: 51 Swahili Phrases in 11 Minutes | Learn Swahili for Beginners (Dating & Romance)
description:
Learn 51 essential Swahili phrases in 11 minutes - the fun, fast way.
#Swahili #LearnSwahili #LanguageLearning

Every phrase follows the same rhythm: hear it in English, hear it in Kiswahili, then say it out loud with the pronunciation guide. Perfect for beginners, travellers and anyone who wants to speak Swahili with confidence.

WHAT YOU GET
- 8 themed chapters, 51 real-life phrases
- Kiswahili audio from a native voice
- English pronunciation guide for every line
- A brand-new lesson every single day

CHAPTERS
0:07  Dating & Romance · Uchumba na Mapenzi
1:28  Family & Home · Familia na Nyumbani
2:55  Phone Calls & Messages · Simu na Ujumbe
4:23  Balance · Usawa
5:40  Wisdom · Hekima
7:01  Inspiration · Msukumo
8:19  Self Improvement · Kujiboresha
9:34  Shopping & Prices · Ununuzi na Bei

PHRASE LIST

DATING & ROMANCE · Uchumba na Mapenzi
• I like how you talk to me. - Ninapenda jinsi unavyozungumza nami.  [Ninapenda JINSI unavoZUNGUMZa NAMi.]
• We should go for coffee tomorrow. - Tunaweza kwenda kwenye kahawa kesho.  [TUNAWEZA KWENda KWAENye kaHAwa KESho.]
• Are you seeing someone right now? - Je, una mtu mwingine sasa hivi?  [Je, uNA mtu MWINgine SAza HIVI?]
• What do you do on weekends? - Unafanya nini wikendi hii?  [UNAfaYA NINI wiKENdi hii?]
• You make me feel calm. - Unanifanya nijisikie tulivu.  [uNANiFAya nijisiKIE TUlivu.]
• I’m not in a rush, really. - Siko katika haraka, kweli.  [SIko kaTIKA haRAka, KEli.]
• Can I hold your hand? - Naomba kushika mkono wako.  [NaOMba kuSHIka MKOno WAko.]

FAMILY & HOME · Familia na Nyumbani
• I’m bringing dinner for everyone. - Ninaleta chakula cha jioni kwa kila mtu.  [NA naleta cha KUU la cha jio NI kwa KILA mtu]
• Where do we keep the spare keys? - Tunaweka funguo za ziada wapi?  [TU naweka FUN guo za ZI ada wAPI]
• Can you help me with the laundry? - Unaweza kunisaidia kufua nguo, tafadhali.  [U NA weza ku NISAIDIA ku FUA nguO, ta FADHILI]
• The kids are asleep, shh please. - Watoto wamelala, shh tafadhali.  [WA to to wa ME lala, shh ta FADHILI]
• Our house smells like fresh bread. - Nyumbani kwetu kunanuka mkate mpya.  [NYUM baani kwa E tu ku NA nuka Mka te MPYA]
• I’ll call Mom after work. - Nitampigia mama simu baada ya kazi.  [NITAM pigia MA ma SI mu baa daa ya KA zi]
• Let’s set the table together. - Tuweke meza pamoja sasa.  [TU Weke ME za pa MOJA sa SA]

PHONE CALLS & MESSAGES · Simu na Ujumbe
• Hi, I’m calling to check in. - Habari, na piga simu kukujulia hali.  [HABARI, na PIGA SIMU kuKujulia haLI.]
• Can you call me back, please? - Unaweza kunipigia simu tena, tafadhali?  [UnaWEZA kuNIPIGIA SIMU teNA, tafadhali?]
• I left you a voicemail. - Nimeacha ujumbe wa simu kwenye kasha la sauti.  [niMEACHA uJUMBE wa SIMU kwenye KAsha la SAUTI.]
• Text me when you’re free. - Nitumie ujumbe ukipata muda.  [niTUMie uJUMBE uKIPATA MUDA.]
• Did you get my message? - Umeupokea ujumbe wangu?  [uMEUPOKEA uJUMBE wangu?]
• I’m stuck in traffic, sorry. - Nimekwama kwenye msongamano wa magari, samahani.  [niMEKWAMA kwenye mSONGOamano wa MAGAri, saMAhani.]
• Let me know if you can make it. - Nijulishe kama unaweza kufika.  [niJULISHE kaMA uKUNA faKIka.]

BALANCE · Usawa
• I need balance in my day. - Nahitaji usawa katika siku yangu.  [NAnahitaji USAWA katika SIKU yangu.]
• Let’s slow down and steady up. - Hebu tupunguze mwendo, tujiweke sawa.  [HEbu tuPUNGuze MwenDO, tujiKEwe SAwa.]
• I balance work and rest. - Nawasawisha kazi na mapumziko.  [NawaSAWiSHa KAzi na maPUMziKO.]
• Even my budget needs balance. - Hata bajeti yangu inahitaji usawa.  [HATA BAjeTI yangu iNAYohitaji USAWA.]
• Keep your life in harmony. - Weka maisha yako yakiwa na usawa.  [WEka maiSHA yaKO yakiwa na USAWA.]
• I’m learning to listen calmly. - Nafunza kusikiliza kwa utulivu, bila kukimbizana.  [NAfunza kuSIKiliZa kwa uTULIvu, bila kuKIMbiZANa.]

WISDOM · Hekima
• Wise choices start with small habits. - Hekima huanza na mazoea madogo.  [HEkima HUanza na maZOEa maDOGO.]
• Think before you speak, always. - Fikiria kabla ya kuongea, kila wakati.  [FI ki riA kaBLA ya kuO ngea, KIla WA ki ti.]
• Choose peace, even when it's hard. - Chagua amani, hata ikiuma.  [CHaGUA aMAni, haTA iKiuMA.]
• Learn fast, but be patient. - Jifunze haraka, lakini subiri kwa upole.  [jiFUNZE haRAka, LAkiNi subiRI kwa uPO le.]
• When unsure, ask one good question. - Ukikosa uhakika, uliza swali moja zuri.  [uKI kOsa uHA ki ka, uLIza SWA li MOja ZU ri.]
• Good advice comes with clear boundaries. - Ushauri mzuri huja na mipaka iliyo wazi.  [ushaURI mzU ri HUja na MI pa ka iLIyo waZI.]

INSPIRATION · Msukumo
• Keep going, even when it’s messy - Endelea hata hali ikiwa changamani.  [En-DE-LEA haa-ti hali i-ki-wa changa-ma-ni.]
• Small steps build big courage - Hatua ndogo hujenga ujasiri mkubwa.  [HA-ta u ndogo hu-JEN-ga u-ja-SI-ri mkU-bwa.]
